items.text: All Aboard!
Guests pour out from inside the inn, producing a bustling commotion livelier than when they first arrived.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Not sure I understand all the fuss. This seems like nothing more than a temporary outage.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: It should be over quickly.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: How come the grid is so doggy? It's done in just by a few speakers and an old vinyl player!

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: I'd suggest an alternative explanation. It looks like the authorities have set up a cordon around what appears to be the town's power plant.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Just our luck, eh?
She removes her sunglasses and surveys the surroundings.
A crowd of young people lingers across the street, whispering to one another.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Any idea what they're on about, Mr. APPLe?

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: This APPLe can only make out the words "Order of Enlightenment" ...

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: The Order of Enlightenment, yeah? Riley mentioned them too. What's their deal?
The term from an unfamiliar era leaves Regulus scratching her head.

items.speaker: Young Man
items.text: It wasn't us, man! This is total crap!

items.speaker: Enforcer I
items.text: Well, whether it was or wasn't, you're coming with us.

items.speaker: Young Man
items.text: On what charge? I know my rights! You can't just haul us to jail for nothing!
The young people are soon flanked on each side by uniformed thugs; there's a tension in the air that would match the best standoff of any spaghetti western.

items.speaker: Enforcer I
items.text: We've had our eyes on you punks for a while now. Under the revised Gold Dust Morality Act, you're suspected of organizing an illegal rock performance.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: What! This is it. We're not letting these thugs get away with arresting these kids!

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Wait, Captain ...
The crowd outside the hotel has gone eerily quiet as they watch the growing ranks of black-uniformed enforcers on the street.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Discretion may be the better part of valor at this moment.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Discretion, mate? Don't you know me better than that?
The tension seems set to break when the moment is interrupted by the appearance of a sharp-dressed man that promptly strides up to the line of black-suited enforcers.
And just like that, the tension fizzles away as the young rockers hang their heads.

items.speaker: Enforcer I
items.text: See, there's nothing to worry about, son. Let's just do this nice and easy.

items.speaker: Enforcer I
items.text: Come along with us. The mayor would like a word. This won't take long.

items.speaker: Young Man
items.text: Damn it. Whatever. Just don't touch me. I can walk there myself.
As the commotion fades into a dejected whimper, the sharp-dressed man turns abruptly and makes a beeline for Regulus.
Ah, a new face. What a blessed young lady.

items.speaker: Mayor Jonathan
items.text: My name is Jonathan, Mayor and Chief Representative of the Order of Enlightenment in this town. We'll be hosting a gathering at the Broadcast Theater tonight.

items.speaker: Mayor Jonathan
items.text: I do hope to see you there, Miss.
The gentleman offers her a handwritten invitation; the fresh ink seems tinged in an oddly ominous hue.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: What's this about, eh? Some kind of show?

items.speaker: Mayor Jonathan
items.text: Of sorts, yes. It's our weekly Sunday hymnal, where we come together to lift our voices in praise.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: In praise ... to who?
She lowers her sunglasses to scan the invitation, catching her tongue on a particular title.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: "The Sufferer"?

items.speaker: Mayor Jonathan
items.text: Yes, the Sufferer. We gather to sing praises for THEIR sake.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: So, you and all your little rozzers are going to be tilting your heads back and warbling for this "Sufferer" guy?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Like Vertin and her little followers singing in a choir in school?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: You couldn't catch me breathing at something as dullsville as all that.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Thanks, but no thanks, mate.

items.speaker: Mayor Jonathan
items.text: A shame to hear that, Miss, especially as a fellow arcanist.

items.speaker: Mayor Jonathan
items.text: If you change your mind, you're always welcome among us.
The gentleman's gaze lingers meaningfully on the floating apple beside her.

items.speaker: Mayor Jonathan
items.text: And that goes for every arcanist.

items.speaker: Mayor Jonathan
items.text: I do hope you and your—"Mr. APPLe" was it?—will be submitting those registration papers soon.

items.speaker: Mayor Jonathan
items.text: Have a pleasant stay here in Gold Dust. All we ask is that you mind our town's ordinances. If you find yourself needing any assistance, do feel free to drop by the theater to see us.

items.speaker: Mayor Jonathan
items.text: The Order of Enlightenment is always eager to assist.
The strange gentleman offers an odd bow, leaning on his cane, and hobbles off as the rest of his enforcers disperse.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Bit of a creep, eh?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Order of Enlightenment? So this mayor is some kind of arcanist extremist; I wonder if Vertin and the Foundation might want to know about these guys.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: You ever hear of this lot, Mr. APPLe?

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: This APPLe hasn't heard the name before, Captain. My apologies.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: No prize for guessing this town's dodgy rules are their doing.

items.speaker: Riley
items.text: Hey, Regulus!
A familiar face waves to her from across the street.
And just as quickly races to meet her.

items.speaker: Riley
items.text: Looks like your apple friend survived! Pleasure to meet you.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: This APPLe is likewise charmed, I'm sure.

items.speaker: Riley
items.text: Oh, and he's got manners too!
She suppresses a laugh. It's not every day she greets a talking apple.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: She's the top bird that gave us a lift.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Good luck that she stopped when she did, or else I might've had to use that disk.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: You're a veritable hero, Miss.

items.speaker: Riley
items.text: Hmm, what did you just say about a disk?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Oh, it's a portable teleportation disk.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: It's all on frequency; I was told it's permitted for use under the Foundation's Public Security Law.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Well, that's what they told me anyway. I never bothered reading them.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: In essence, the guidelines dictate that all registered arcanists constrain themselves to pre-approved arcane skills.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: It's a matter of ensuring that arcanum is used for the good of all.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Though that part ... seems to have fallen by the wayside lately.
APPLe concludes his statement on a low note, but it seems not to have thrown off the groove of his compatriots.

items.speaker: Riley
items.text: Blah, blah. All I know is rules are meant to be broken, haha.

items.speaker: Riley
items.text: Especially if breaking said dumb rule doesn't do any harm.
She flourishes her statement with a laugh before popping a piece of chocolate in her mouth.

items.speaker: Riley
items.text: See? Is there anybody in the world that's put out over me having a bite of chocolate?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Smashing, love. Good to see I've found a fellow rebel.

items.speaker: Riley
items.text: And not just one. We've got a whole bunch.
She holds out a chocolate ball, as if offering a badge of office.

items.speaker: Riley
items.text: So, you in?

items.speaker: Riley
items.text: We're planning something fun—to bring a little excitement to this boring old town!
The two kindred spirits lock eyes; there is no question in Regulus's mind.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: You can count on me, pal.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Oh! Make that count on us!

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: This APPLe need not say more. We're with you, Ms. Riley.
He bobs up and down in the air as a show of courtesy.

items.speaker: Riley
items.text: Alright, catch you two later.
